name: Madagascar Sign Language
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: But it is prosodically different from IX. An IX gets a word stress. But a GEN is an enclitic to the preceding sign, i.e. a noun if it is genitive and a verb if it is ergative. The host sign and the enclitic GEN are pronounced in one go like a compound and the GEN does not get a word stress and is dependent on the host prosodically. [p. 56] ... The genitive pronominal signs are enclitics and are different from other IX signs. They are signed in one go with the previous signs like compounds in a way. In other words, they are prosodically dependent on the previous signs and do not get an independent word stress assigned. [n. 11, p. 67]
new_statements.citation: Minoura, Nobukatsu. 2008. Word Order in Malagasy Sign Language (TTM). Tōkyō gaikokugo daigaku ronshū / Area and Culture Studies 77: 47-69. Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. doi:10.15026/50377, hdl:10108/50377
new_statements.locator: p. 56, section 3.1.7 (ergative-case marking); restated in endnote 11, p. 67
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (23 pp., the PDF's metadata gives the title "Word Order in Malagasy Sign Language (TTM)") via the kept page images ocr2008/printed p. 56) and ocr2008/printed p. 67) and the scanned text. Both quoted passages are on the page images exactly as quoted: p. 56, sec. 3.1.7 "Ergative marking": "But it is prosodically different from IX. An IX gets a word stress. But a GEN is an enclitic to the preceding sign, i.e. a noun if it is genitive and a verb if it is ergative. The host sign and the enclitic GEN are pronounced in one go like a compound and the GEN does not get a word stress and is dependent on the host prosodically." (followed by "And in some cases GEN copies the handshape of the host…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Sign language (visual-manual modality). The only statement about 'word stress' is that each prosodically independent sign (e.g. an index/pronoun IX) carries its own word stress, whereas the genitive/ergative pronominal enclitic GEN is signed together with its host 'in one go like a compound' and receives no word stress. This is a statement about prosodic-word status (free sign vs. enclitic), not about a position within a word; no source gives a positional or weight-based rule, and none of the fixed spoken-language readings applies.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the enclitic GEN may also copy the handshape of its host (p. 56).
new_statements.domain_note: Word/compound level: host sign + enclitic form one prosodic unit. Data are elicited TTM sentences from deaf consultants (Mme Eva and others, Antananarivo). Minoura 2014 (n. 18, p. 114) states explicitly that phonetic and phonological analysis of TTM has not yet been undertaken, so no fuller stress description exists in print.
new_statements.identity_note: mada1271 is a SIGN LANGUAGE (Malagasy Sign Language, Tenin'ny Tanana Malagasy, TTM; ISO 639-3 mzc; Danish/Norwegian-SL-influenced, first deaf school Antsirabe 1960). The quoted statement is about signs, not spoken syllables: 'word stress' in Minoura 2008 means the prosodic independence of a free sign versus an enclitic pronoun sign. Data are from Antananarivo-area deaf consultants; Minoura 2018b discusses variation between 'narrow' TTM and other signing in Madagascar but names no separate glottocode.
